Call reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="strict"): strict IS the default, so the error mode is exactly equivalent to having no guard at all -- yet it looks identical to the real thing.

small_sample_disclosure.why: #46: I nearly published a MAGNITUDE taken from a single cell with n=3. The headline 'multi scores 9.5 points lower' came entirely from F4, where multi was 1/3 and baseline 3/3 -- and a same-config rerun of the BASELINE on that same scenario produced 2/3. With three rounds a per-scenario accuracy can only take 0/33/67/100, so adjacent rungs are 33 points apart: that resolution cannot support a 9.5-point claim. The fix has two halves: soften the wording everywhere, and make the RUNNER say it out loud (the half a test can hold on to).

keyword_inflection.why: #48: the keyword matcher compared plain substrings, so F4's criterion keyword 'retry' could not match 'retries' -- 'retries' neither contains 'retry' (it is 'retri'+'es') nor starts with it. Measured consequence: an answer that NAMED THE EXACT PARAMETER (W_INVENTORY_DOWNSTREAM_RETRIES) and described the amplification was scored as 'never mentioned retries'. It hit both sides (one multi round, one baseline round), and the baseline round's text WAS the declared answer. This is the fifth occurrence of the 'keywords cannot keep up with real language' family (#16/#21/#28), and the first one with a precise mechanism: English inflection. The fix normalises English word forms on BOTH sides (keyword and text), keeps substring matching for Chinese, and the dismissal logic is untouched -- a widening fix must not resurrect the old false positives.

unsupported_claim_diagnostic.why: #44: the coordinator promoted a QUIET metric with no baseline comparison (inventory stock_level, which is the normal fixture remainder) to a root cause, and simultaneously dropped the real one. I tried twice to turn that phenomenon into a number. Variant 1 ('any clause that does not match the declared truth') measured 11 for multi vs 9 for baseline -- it also counted supporting observations, so it does not discriminate: a metric that hits both sides equally is noise. Variant 2 (adding 'metric-shaped token' + 'anomaly wording') measured 4 vs 0 and LOOKED discriminating, but it worked by accident (the real texts happen to contain the word for 'water level'), and my own synthetic control case destroyed it: the realistic form {SKU-001}=998092 does not match the regex I wrote. Following the #32 precedent, I did NOT ship a misleading metric. What ships is the precise half: how many of the causes the answer ITSELF lists do not match the scenario's declared truth -- a precision diagnostic, measured at multi 11 / baseline 9, explicitly NOT a discriminator. #44 therefore stays yellow.
